subject: Post-call: procurement sync — PO vs card, marketplace pilot & next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@solarahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: procurement sync — PO vs card, marketplace pilot & next steps

Rajiv — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so your team has what it needs to evaluate commercial pathing.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- AP policy: there is a threshold for PO vs card — need to confirm whether it is per-invoice or monthly cap. You mentioned current default is PO for larger vendors but there are card exceptions for pilots.
- Marketplace preference: Solara prefers purchases via Azure Marketplace where possible to speed onboarding and avoid legal review, but vendor listing requirements are a gating factor.
- Vendor onboarding: your team requires W-9, certificate of insurance, and vendor setup in Coupa. Additional security questionnaire may be requested for production access.

What we can do immediately:
1) Attach our Redwood_Onboarding_Packet.pdf (vendor packet + standard MSA + W-9 + COI template).
2) Produce a price breakout by line item and a pilot proposal sized to fit a card payment (to reduce procurement friction).
3) Share marketplace onboarding checklist and confirm whether Redwood can list on Azure Marketplace under Solara subscription/offer.

Asks / next steps:
- Rajiv / Lisa: can you confirm the AP threshold that triggers PO vs card (per invoice amount and/or monthly cumulative)?
- If marketplace is preferred, what exact marketplace are you targeting (Azure / AWS Marketplace)? Any marketplace-specific docs we should complete?
- We'll propose a short Friday window (30 minutes) to run through the vendor packet and pilot pricing; please share availability.

Tagged attachments: Redwood_Onboarding_Packet.pdf (vendor packet, sample MSA, W-9, COI).

Thanks — happy to jump on a procurement-only call if that helps.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
O: (415) 555-0182 | evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

--
Redwood Onboarding Packet (attached): Redwood_Onboarding_Packet.pdf
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@solarahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Mendez <finance@solarahealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement sync — PO vs card, marketplace pilot & next steps

Evelyn — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from AP / procurement: 
- Thresholds: our current policy treats any single invoice > $10,000 as PO-required. Monthly cumulative limits may push a vendor into PO as well, but the line-item threshold is the primary trigger.
- Card exceptions: for pilots under $5k / month we can often accept card, but it requires finance sign-off and a short vendor risk review.
- Marketplace: Solara uses the Azure Marketplace for most SaaS; if Redwood can publish an offer there it reduces the need for full Coupa onboarding. We still require marketplace seller verification and a billing mapping document.

Attached is our initial vendor requirements workbook (solara_vendor_requirements.xlsx). It lists the documents we need for Coupa and for marketplace listing.

Next steps from our side:
1) Please provide a 1-2 page price breakout + a pilot SKU that fits under the $5k card-exception threshold.
2) If you can publish to Azure Marketplace, include estimated time-to-list and any third-party fees.
3) We'll aim to pull in finance for a short call — Friday between 9–11am PT works for Lisa and me. Is that doable?

Thanks —
Rajiv Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager | Solara Health
rajiv.patel@solarahealth.com
(617) 555-0224

Attachment: solara_vendor_requirements.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-call: procurement sync — PO vs card, marketplace pilot & next steps

Eve / Karthik — quick internal note: I can draft the pilot pricing and a price_breakout_v1.xlsx today. Proposal: two options — (A) 3-month pilot sized at $4,500/month billed via card to avoid the PO path, (B) annual commitment with PO for standard discounting. For the marketplace path, I’ll enumerate costs and estimated time-to-list (usually 3–4 weeks if we have seller verification completed).

I recommend pushing the pilot via card + marketplace concurrently: pilot on card (fast) + start marketplace onboarding to transition to marketplace billing for production. This reduces time-to-value and keeps the procurement team comfortable.

I’ll share drafts by EOD.

— Marcus
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@solarahealth.com>, Lisa Mendez <finance@solarahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement sync — PO vs card, marketplace pilot & next steps

Rajiv / Lisa — thanks, that timing works. Confirming next steps and owners: 

1) Redwood (Evelyn): sending price_breakout_v1.xlsx (pilot + annual options) and the vendor packet we discussed. Attached: price_breakout_v1.xlsx, marketplace_onboard_checklist.pdf.
2) Redwood (Marcus): will include estimated time-to-list and third-party fees for Azure Marketplace; will highlight a pilot SKU at ~$4.5k/month to fit the card exception.
3) Solara (Rajiv / Lisa): confirm final AP threshold (you noted $10k per invoice) and whether finance will sign-off for a sub-$5k pilot on card during Friday's call.

Proposed meeting: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 @ 09:30am PT — 30 minutes. I'll send a calendar invite with agenda (vendor packet walk-through + pilot acceptance criteria).

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: price_breakout_v1.xlsx, marketplace_onboard_checklist.pdf
